description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 1) as the whole of t/re/reg_email.t:
perl produces 13 rows, PCL prints `1..0` and nothing else, and the file has no
abort and no diagnostic.

perl's `DATA` handle IS THE SOURCE FILE, positioned just past the `__DATA__`
line.  So the rewind idiom perl's own tests use --

    seek *DATA, 0, 0;                          # back to the top of the FILE
    while (<DATA>) { last if /^__DATA__/ }     # skip forward again
    while (<DATA>) { ... the rows ... }

-- works there.  PCL installs DATA as a string-input-stream over ONLY the text
after `__DATA__` (`%p-install-fh` / `make-string-input-stream text`,
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), so `seek DATA,0,0` rewinds to the start of the DATA TEXT,
the rescan loop consumes all of it without ever seeing a `__DATA__` line, and
the second loop reads nothing.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s473t5e/probe-data-seek.pl), a file with three data lines:

                                    perl   PCL
    first pass rows                 3      3
    lines read looking for __DATA__ 19     3     <- perl re-reads the FILE
    second pass rows                3      0
    first row of the second pass    alpha  (none)

ROWS: t/re/reg_email.t, 13 rows short (the file's whole plan).  reg_email.t is
also the reason `re/reg_email_thr.t` exists -- its comment says the seek "is
necessary with PERLIO=stdio when this test is run from another thread".

FIX SHAPE: install DATA over the WHOLE source text with its position set just
past the `__DATA__` line, instead of over the tail alone.  Then `seek`, `tell`
and `-s` all answer as perl does, and the ordinary `while (<DATA>)` is
unchanged because the initial position is the same place.  The text is already
in hand at that point (the transpiler has read the source), so this is a
change of WHAT is stored plus an initial `file-position`, not new machinery.

CHECK WHEN DOING IT: `tell(DATA)` before any read (perl gives the byte offset
of the first data line, not 0) and a `__END__`-instead-of-`__DATA__` file, which
perl treats identically in `main`.  And whether any shipped module reads DATA
-- `grep -al '<DATA>' lib/` -- so the change is measured against those too.
subject: the `DATA` handle holds only the text AFTER `__DATA__`, so `seek DATA,0,0` rewinds to the start of that text where perl rewinds the SOURCE FILE -- the `seek`+rescan-for-`__DATA__` idiom yields ZERO rows (t/re/reg_email.t, 13 rows)
